speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) in the past three years, how many domestic violence cases against women, especially those above 50 years, have been reported; (b) what is the Ministry doing to reach out to those who may be suffering in silence; and (c) whether the Ministry will look into ways to raise public awareness and work with grassroots groups to reach out to the silent victims.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: A strong partnership among Government agencies and community partners is necessary to ensure that those affected by violence receive the needed help and receive it early.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The National Family Violence Networking System (NFVNS) was established more than 20 years ago for victims to be assisted by touchpoints, such as Family Service Centres and Family Violence Specialist Centres.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is why, Mr Speaker, Sir, you will remember that you had launched the "Break the Silence Against Family Violence" campaign for the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) last year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This campaign raises awareness about family violence through platforms, such as social media and community roadshows.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It also involves collaboration with community and corporate partners to equip bystanders with resources and skills to safely step in to help victims.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We train partners and grassroots organisations to understand family violence and, importantly, to identify families experiencing violence early.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Recently, MSF facilitated a conversation with Taman Jurong Citizens’ Consultative Committee (CCC), Fei Yue Family Service Centre, Jurong West Neighbourhood Police Centre and SSO@Taman Jurong on ways to prevent and intervene in family violence situations together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This saw participation from grassroots leaders, schools, arts and sports groups, corporate bodies, self-help groups, the Ng Teng Fong General Hospital and the Police.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Such initiatives deepen the awareness of family violence and enable more people to break the silence and reach out to seek help for those affected.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Recently, I had a meeting with three voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) in my constituency and all the three reported that there is an upward trend in the cases that they handle on violence against women who are above 50 years old.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: All the three consistently said the same thing.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask, nationally, is this the trend?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question: will there be a study commissioned to see what the root cause is and how we can intervene for these violence cases against elderly women?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But every case is one case too many and we remain concerned about addressing the key issues that lead to violence in families, especially violence against women and violence against seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But family members, relatives, neighbours, colleagues, community leaders, friends can help to spot what would otherwise be an invisible problem and help alert the many touchpoints that are available that would allow us to intervene.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In situations where people do not seek help but we are alerted to family violence, the Member would know that MSF is working on a Vulnerable Adults Bill with laws that would allow us to intervene in such instances.
